text:
michael: Quick heads-up — ran a profiling sweep on the 16-GPU TP+PP config (2TP x 8PP) with microbatch=8, seq=2048. Noticed PP bubble growth in steady state.
anya: Can you paste the flamegraph or a short summary?
michael: profiler-bot: https://artifacts.redwood/prof/1716777777/fg.svg (flamegraph + stage timing CSV)
michael: TL;DR: all-reduce wall time per step increased after the driver/kernel bump. Numbers below.
michael: before (fused_allreduce): allreduce=2.1ms, fragments=3, bubble≈0.9ms. After (same workload, new kernel): allreduce=5.6ms, fragments=9, bubble≈6ms.
lia: Huh — fused_allreduce should reduce latency. Are we fragmenting more due to batching change?
michael: Looks like fragmentation + increased KV cache misses. raw log extract: 
```
allreduce_bytes=48MB fragments=3 latency_ms=2.1
allreduce_bytes=48MB fragments=9 latency_ms=5.6
kv_cache_miss_rate=4% -> 22%
```
rahul: 22% miss rate is huge. Why did cache miss rate spike when mb=8?
michael: microbatch expansion changed the token alignment/padding heuristic; many requests now hit different tile boundaries causing less prefix reuse.
anya: That explains lost comm/compute overlap — more recompute + more fragments => less async overlap.
michael: Quick experiments: microbatch=4 -> steady bubble < 1ms; microbatch=8 -> bubble ~6-8ms and throughput slightly higher but inefficient. 1F1B schedule with strict staggering reduces bubble but throughput drops ~4%.
lia: Which stage is the bottleneck? We saw stage3 (attention-heavy) getting overloaded in the profile.
michael: stage timings: stage2=21.2ms, stage3=28.7ms, stage4=21.0ms. Stage3 had largest queue and most fragmented allreduces.
rahul: Two risky angles: kernel selection heuristic and stage-local microbatch caps. Also check whether the new kernel disables async gpu copies.
michael: I dug into kernel flags — the generic kernel path fell back to synchronous allreduce when fragments>6 under the new runtime. Switching to async_cuMemcpy cut stall by ~2ms in a micro test.
anya: Can we sketch a short heuristic?
michael: pseudo: 
```
if fragments > 4:
  prefer = split_allreduce
elif kv_miss_rate > 10%:
  prefer = split_allreduce
else:
  prefer = fused_allreduce
```
michael: Proposed plan: 1) introduce a kernel-selection toggle that prefers split_allreduce when fragments or KV miss high, 2) add adaptive microbatch cap per pipeline stage (stage-local cap), 3) implement lightweight KV prefetch for last 2 timesteps to reduce misses.
lia: +1 for adaptive microbatch per stage. We have data showing stage imbalance — capping stage3 improved overlap previously.
rahul: I'll prototype a split_allreduce experiment and add an async copy path test. Also will add a perf matrix to run automated sweeps.
michael: I'll run a canary with split_allreduce + stage-local mb caps.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: starting canary: 2 nodes, tag=pp-shadowrun-1716777777, config=split_allreduce+stage-mb-cap
michael: canary kicked at 1716777800, running 50 iters warmup then 2k steady iters.
profiler-bot: initial 50 iters: mean step time 24.3ms -> 22.8ms when using split_allreduce; bubble reduced from ~5.9ms -> ~2.2ms (KV prefetch OFF). Need longer run.
anya: promising. If split_allreduce + caps keep bubble <=2ms for pp8, we can gate behind a feature flag.
lia: agree. Add flag + metric to rollouts dashboard (bubble_ms_p90, kv_miss_rate).
rahul: I'll add perf-compare job for matrix: microbatch in [4,8,12], seq in [1024,2048], fragments in [1,4,8,12]. Will collect bubble p50/p90, allreduce ms, kv_miss.
michael: Also note: when async_cuMemcpy enabled, stage3 stall drops ~2ms — include that toggle in the canary.
anya: Can someone own a 24h canary? need stability + memory regressions check.
michael: I'll run 24h if the 2hr looks stable. Uploading logs + flamegraphs to the issue: https://issues.internal/RED-pp-shadowrun-1716
lia: :thumbsup: thanks for the quick sleuthing.
rahul: on it — will file PRs for kernel-heuristic toggle + perf job.
anya: leaving a postmortem-ish note in the issue about driver/kernel compatibility next to the rollout checklist.
michael: cool. I’ll follow up with concrete numbers in the issue and attach csv of the perf matrix.
lia: If this lands, we should update the model-serving docs to recommend microbatch defaults per PP size.
michael: Agreed.
anya: tagging @eng-platform for visibility.
lia: noted.
profiler-bot: will schedule overnight extended run and report by morning.
